newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: SOCCER-PARAGUAY CLOSE TO WORLD CUP AFTER BEATING URUGUAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARAGUAY CLOSE TO WORLD CUP AFTER BEATING URUGUAY.

text.p: Paraguay almost certainly assured itself a place in next year's World Cup by beating former greats Uruguay 3-1 in a South American World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
The result left two-times world champions Uruguay in severe danger of missing out on the World Cup finals for the second successive time.
Uruguay played with ten men from the 17th minute after midfielder Alvaro Guttierez was sent off for kicking an opponent.

Aristides Rojas put Paraguay in front before halftime and second half goals from Jose Cardozo, who converted a penalty, and substitute Derlis Soto put the game beyond Uruguay's reach. Dario Silva scored a late consolation.

Paraguay top the single South American group with 23 points from ten games and, with the top four of the nine teams qualifying, enjoy a ten-point advantage over the side in fifth place. Uruguay have 13 points from ten games.
Paraguay, who last qualified in 1986, were without their top player, volatile goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert.
Chilavert, who also takes his team's free kicks and penalties, was suspended for four games on Tuesday for fighting after being sent off against Colombia earlier this month.
Paraguayan defender Catalino Rivarola was sent off in the last minute and will also miss the team's next game, at home to Argentina on July 6.
Paraguay, who won their fifth straight home match in the competition, were fast and competitive but never spectacular.
Derlis Soto, who scored the winner against Colombia, came on as a substitute in the first half and provided the cross from which Rojas opened the scoring with a near-post header in the 37th minute.
Uruguay, with veteran playermaker Enzo Francescoli short of inspiration, had started promisingly but lost the midfield battle after the departure of Gutierrez.
Cardozo increased Paraguay's lead in the 73rd minute after Rojas had been tripped and ten minutes later Soto scrambled in the third, to the delight of a packed house.
Silva's consolation came in the 87th minute.

Paraguay - 22-Ruben Ruiz Diaz, 3-Catalino Rivarola, 5-Celso Ayala, 4-Carlos Gamarra, 14-Juan Villamayor, 20-Julio Enciso (16-Derlis Soto, 32), 10-Roberto Acuna, 6-Estanislao Struway, 15-Miguel Benitez (19-Virgilio Ferreira, 58), 18-Aristides Rojas (17-Hugo Brizuela, 76), 9-Jose Cardozo.

Uruguay - 1-Robert Siboldi, 2-Gustavo Mendez, 4-Jose Herrera, 3-Eber Moas, 13-Leonardo Ramos, 11-Gustavo Poyet, 5- Alvaro Guterrez, 6-Gonzalo de los Santos, 10-Enzo Francescoli, 17-Sergio Martinez (8-Pablo Bengoechea, 42), 7-Marcelo Otero (20-Dario Silva, 65).
